source.note: Scan without a text layer. National Senior Certificate paper (cover: NATIONAL SENIOR CERTIFICATE; running header: NSC). The PDF includes the cover (printed page 1), the instructions (page 2) and the information sheet (page 16); PDF page n = printed page n. The cover states that the question paper consists of 15 pages, 1 information sheet and an answer book of 31 pages, which is not in this PDF. Duration 3 hours as printed on the cover. Source file and hash are recorded in sources/maths/manifest.json.

extraction.method: manual transcription from 170 dpi page renders, checked at 400 dpi where needed

questions.stem_md: The cumulative frequency graph (ogive) drawn below shows the total number of food items ordered from a menu over a period of 1 hour.

questions.text_md: Write down the total number of food items ordered from the menu during this hour.
Write down the modal class of the data.
How long did it take to order the first $30$ food items?
How many food items were ordered in the last $15$ minutes?
Determine the $75^{\mathrm{th}}$ percentile for the data.
Calculate the interquartile range of the data.

questions.stem_md: Reggie works part-time as a waiter at a local restaurant. The amount of money (in rands) he made in tips over a $15$-day period is given below.
Calculate:

questions.text_md: (a)  The mean of the data
(b)  The standard deviation of the data

questions.stem_md:
Mary also works part-time as a waitress at the same restaurant. Over the same $15$-day period Mary collected the same mean amount in tips as Reggie, but her standard deviation was R$14$.

Using the available information, comment on the:

questions.text_md: (a)  Total amount in tips that they EACH collected over the $15$-day period
(b)  Variation that EACH of them received in daily tips over this period

questions.stem_md: A familiar question among professional tennis players is whether the speed of a tennis serve (in km/h) depends on the height of a player (in metres). The heights of $21$ tennis players and the average speed of their serves were recorded during a tournament. The data is represented in the scatter plot below. The least squares regression line is also drawn.

questions.text_md: Write down the fastest average serve speed (in km/h) achieved in this tournament.

questions.stem_md:
Consider the following correlation coefficients:

A.  $r=0,93$\qquad B.  $r=-0,42$\qquad C.  $r=0,52$

questions.text_md: Which ONE of the given correlation coefficients best fits the plotted data?
Use the scatter plot and least squares regression line to motivate your answer to QUESTION $2.2.1$.
What does the data suggest about the speed of a tennis serve (in km/h) and the height of a player (in metres)?

The equation of the regression line is given as $\hat{y}=27,07+bx$.
Explain why, in this context, the least squares regression line CANNOT intersect the $y$-axis at $(0\,;\,27,07)$.

questions.stem_md: In the diagram, $\mathrm{K}(-1\,;\,2)$, $\mathrm{L}$ and $\mathrm{N}(1\,;\,-1)$ are vertices of $\triangle\mathrm{KLN}$ such that $\mathrm{L}\hat{\mathrm{K}}\mathrm{N}=78,69^{\circ}$. $\mathrm{KL}$ intersects the $x$-axis at $\mathrm{P}$. $\mathrm{KL}$ is produced. The inclination of $\mathrm{KN}$ is $\theta$. The coordinates of $\mathrm{M}$ are $(-3\,;\,-5)$.
Calculate:

questions.text_md: The gradient of $\mathrm{KN}$
The size of $\theta$, the inclination of $\mathrm{KN}$
Show that the gradient of $\mathrm{KL}$ is equal to $1$.
Determine the equation of the straight line $\mathrm{KL}$ in the form $y=mx+c$.
Calculate the length of $\mathrm{KN}$.

questions.stem_md: It is further given that $\mathrm{KN}=\mathrm{LM}$.

questions.text_md: Calculate the possible coordinates of $\mathrm{L}$.
Determine the coordinates of $\mathrm{L}$ if it is given that $\mathrm{KLMN}$ is a parallelogram.
$\mathrm{T}$ is a point on $\mathrm{KL}$ produced. $\mathrm{TM}$ is drawn such that $\mathrm{TM}=\mathrm{LM}$. Calculate the area of $\triangle\mathrm{KTN}$.
questions.notes: Area of a triangle from coordinates; no dedicated coordinate-area skill. Closest existing skills tagged.

questions.stem_md: In the diagram, the equation of the circle with centre $\mathrm{F}$ is $(x-3)^{2}+(y-1)^{2}=r^{2}$. $\mathrm{S}(6\,;\,5)$ is a point on the circle with centre $\mathrm{F}$. Another circle with centre $\mathrm{G}(m\,;\,n)$ in the $4^{\mathrm{th}}$ quadrant touches the circle with centre $\mathrm{F}$, at $\mathrm{H}$ such that $\mathrm{FH}:\mathrm{HG}=1:2$. The point $\mathrm{J}$ lies in the first quadrant such that $\mathrm{HJ}$ is a common tangent to both these circles. $\mathrm{JK}$ is a tangent to the larger circle at $\mathrm{K}$.

questions.text_md: Write down the coordinates of $\mathrm{F}$.
Calculate the length of $\mathrm{FS}$.
Write down the length of $\mathrm{HG}$.
Give a reason why $\mathrm{JH}=\mathrm{JK}$.

questions.stem_md: Determine:

questions.text_md: The distance $\mathrm{FJ}$, with reasons, if it is given that $\mathrm{JK}=20$
The equation of the circle with centre $\mathrm{G}$ in terms of $m$ and $n$ in the form $(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2}=r^{2}$
The coordinates of $\mathrm{G}$, if it is further given that the equation of tangent $\mathrm{JK}$ is $x=22$

questions.stem_md: In the diagram, $\mathrm{P}(k\,;\,1)$ is a point in the $2^{\mathrm{nd}}$ quadrant and is $\sqrt{5}$ units from the origin. $\mathrm{R}$ is a point on the positive $x$-axis and obtuse $\mathrm{R}\hat{\mathrm{O}}\mathrm{P}=\theta$.

questions.text_md: Calculate the value of $k$.

questions.stem_md: **Without using a calculator**, calculate the value of:

questions.text_md: (a)  $\tan\theta$
(b)  $\cos(180^{\circ}+\theta)$
(c)  $\sin(\theta+60^{\circ})$ in the form $\dfrac{a+b}{\sqrt{20}}$
**Use a calculator** to calculate the value of $\tan(2\theta-40^{\circ})$ correct to ONE decimal place.
Prove the following identity:  $\dfrac{\cos x+\sin x}{\cos x-\sin x}-\dfrac{\cos x-\sin x}{\cos x+\sin x}=2\tan 2x$
Evaluate, **without using a calculator**:  $\displaystyle\sum_{A=38^{\circ}}^{52^{\circ}}\cos^{2}A$
questions.notes: Limits and the squared cosine confirmed at 400 dpi: sum from A=38° to A=52° of cos² A.

questions.stem_md: Consider: $f(x)=-2\tan\dfrac{3}{2}x$

questions.text_md: Write down the period of $f$.
The point $\mathrm{A}(t\,;\,2)$ lies on the graph. Determine the general solution of $t$.

On the grid provided in the ANSWER BOOK, draw the graph of $f$ for the interval $x\in[-120^{\circ}\,;\,180^{\circ}]$. Clearly show ALL asymptotes, intercepts with the axes and endpoint(s) of the graph.
Use the graph to determine for which value(s) of $x$ will $f(x)\ge 2$ for $x\in[-120^{\circ}\,;\,180^{\circ}]$.
Describe the transformation of graph $f$ to form the graph of $g(x)=-2\tan\left(\dfrac{3}{2}x+60^{\circ}\right)$.

questions.stem_md: A pilot is flying in a helicopter. At point $\mathrm{A}$, which is $h$ metres directly above point $\mathrm{D}$ on the ground, he notices a strange object at point $\mathrm{B}$. The pilot determines that the angle of depression from $\mathrm{A}$ to $\mathrm{B}$ is $30^{\circ}$. He also determines that the control room at point $\mathrm{C}$ is $3h$ metres from $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{B}\hat{\mathrm{A}}\mathrm{C}=2x$. Points $\mathrm{B}$, $\mathrm{C}$ and $\mathrm{D}$ are in the same horizontal plane. This scenario is shown in the diagram below.

questions.text_md: Determine the distance $\mathrm{AB}$ in terms of $h$.
Show that the distance between the strange object at point $\mathrm{B}$ and the control room at point $\mathrm{C}$ is given by $\mathrm{BC}=h\sqrt{25-24\cos^{2}x}$.

questions.stem_md:
$\mathrm{PON}$ is a diameter of the circle centred at $\mathrm{O}$. $\mathrm{TM}$ is a tangent to the circle at $\mathrm{M}$, a point on the circle. $\mathrm{R}$ is another point on the circle such that $\mathrm{OR}\parallel\mathrm{PM}$. $\mathrm{NR}$ and $\mathrm{MN}$ are drawn. Let $\hat{\mathrm{M}}_{1}=66^{\circ}$.

Calculate, with reasons, the size of EACH of the following angles:

questions.text_md: $\hat{\mathrm{P}}$
$\hat{\mathrm{M}}_{2}$
$\hat{\mathrm{N}}_{1}$
$\hat{\mathrm{O}}_{2}$
$\hat{\mathrm{N}}_{2}$

questions.stem_md: In the diagram, $\triangle\mathrm{AGH}$ is drawn. $\mathrm{F}$ and $\mathrm{C}$ are points on $\mathrm{AG}$ and $\mathrm{AH}$ respectively such that $\mathrm{AF}=20$ units, $\mathrm{FG}=15$ units and $\mathrm{CH}=21$ units. $\mathrm{D}$ is a point on $\mathrm{FC}$ such that $\mathrm{ABCD}$ is a rectangle with $\mathrm{AB}$ also parallel to $\mathrm{GH}$. The diagonals of $\mathrm{ABCD}$ intersect at $\mathrm{M}$, a point on $\mathrm{AH}$.

questions.text_md: Explain why $\mathrm{FC}\parallel\mathrm{GH}$.
Calculate, with reasons, the length of $\mathrm{DM}$.

questions.stem_md: In the diagram, $\mathrm{JKLM}$ is a cyclic quadrilateral and the circle has centre $\mathrm{O}$.
questions.text_md: Prove the theorem which states that $\hat{\mathrm{J}}+\hat{\mathrm{L}}=180^{\circ}$.

questions.stem_md: In the diagram, a smaller circle $\mathrm{ABTS}$ and a bigger circle $\mathrm{BDRT}$ are given. $\mathrm{BT}$ is a common chord. Straight lines $\mathrm{STD}$ and $\mathrm{ATR}$ are drawn. Chords $\mathrm{AS}$ and $\mathrm{DR}$ are produced to meet in $\mathrm{C}$, a point outside the two circles. $\mathrm{BS}$ and $\mathrm{BD}$ are drawn. $\hat{\mathrm{A}}=x$ and $\hat{\mathrm{R}}_{1}=y$.
Name, giving a reason, another angle equal to:

questions.text_md: Prove that $\mathrm{SCDB}$ is a cyclic quadrilateral.

It is further given that $\hat{\mathrm{D}}_{2}=30^{\circ}$ and $\mathrm{A}\hat{\mathrm{S}}\mathrm{T}=100^{\circ}$.
Prove that $\mathrm{SD}$ is not a diameter of circle $\mathrm{BDS}$.

questions.stem_md: In the diagram, $\mathrm{ABCD}$ is a cyclic quadrilateral such that $\mathrm{AC}\perp\mathrm{CB}$ and $\mathrm{DC}=\mathrm{CB}$. $\mathrm{AD}$ is produced to $\mathrm{M}$ such that $\mathrm{AM}\perp\mathrm{MC}$. Let $\hat{\mathrm{B}}=x$.
Prove that:

questions.text_md: $\mathrm{MC}$ is a tangent to the circle at $\mathrm{C}$
$\triangle\mathrm{ACB}\parallel\triangle\mathrm{CMD}$

questions.stem_md: Hence, or otherwise, prove that:

questions.text_md: $\dfrac{\mathrm{CM}^{2}}{\mathrm{DC}^{2}}=\dfrac{\mathrm{AM}}{\mathrm{AB}}$
$\dfrac{\mathrm{AM}}{\mathrm{AB}}=\sin^{2}x$
